landmarks.name: Chichen Itza
landmarks.writeup: A large pre-Columbian archaeological site built by the Maya civilization, famous for the pyramid of Kukulkan.

wiki.extract: Chichen Itza was a large pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people of the Terminal Classic period. The archeological site is located in Tinúm Municipality, Yucatán, Mexico.

landmarks.name: Teotihuacan
landmarks.writeup: An ancient Mesoamerican city known for its massive Pyramids of the Sun and Moon.

wiki.extract: Teotihuacan is an ancient Mesoamerican city located in a sub-valley of the Valley of Mexico, which is located in the State of Mexico, 40 kilometers (25 mi) northeast of modern-day Mexico City.

landmarks.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
landmarks.writeup: A prominent cultural center in Mexico City known for its architecture and murals.

wiki.extract: The Palacio de Bellas Artes is a prominent cultural center in Mexico City. It hosts performing arts events, literature events and plastic arts galleries and exhibitions. "Bellas Artes" for short, has been called the "art cathedral of Mexico", and is located on the western side of the historic center of Mexico City which is close to the Alameda Central park.

landmarks.name: Copper Canyon
landmarks.writeup: A group of six canyons in the Sierra Madre Occidental, larger and deeper than the Grand Canyon.

wiki.extract: Copper Canyon is a group of six distinct canyons in the Sierra Madre Occidental in the southwestern part of the state of Chihuahua in northwestern Mexico that is 65,000 square kilometres (25,000 sq mi) in size. The canyons were formed by six rivers that drain the western side of the Sierra Tarahumara. All six rivers merge into the Rio Fuerte and empty into the Gulf of California. The walls of the canyon are a copper/green color, which is the origin of the name.

landmarks.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
landmarks.writeup: Also known as La Casa Azul, it is the former home of the famous Mexican artist Frida Kahlo.

wiki.extract: The Frida Kahlo Museum, also known as The Blue House for the structure's cobalt-blue walls, is a historic house museum and art museum dedicated to the life and work of Mexican artist Frida Kahlo. It is in the Colonia del Carmen neighborhood of Coyoacán in Mexico City. The building was Kahlo's birthplace, the home where she grew up, lived with her husband Diego Rivera for a number of years, and where she later died in a room on the upper floor. In 1957, Rivera donated the home and its contents to turn it into a museum in Kahlo's honor.

cultural_events.name: Día de los Muertos
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional festival honoring deceased loved ones with altars, offerings, and celebrations.

wiki.extract: The Day of the Dead is a holiday traditionally celebrated on November 1 and 2, though other days, such as October 31 or November 6, may be included depending on the locality. The multi-day holiday involves family and friends gathering to pay respects and remember friends and family members who have died. The celebrations can take a humorous tone, as celebrants remember amusing events and anecdotes about the departed. The festival is widely observed in Mexico and among people of Mexican heritage in other parts of the world. It falls during the Christian period of Allhallowtide. Some argue that there are Indigenous Mexican or ancient Aztec influences that account for the custom, though others see it as a local expression of the Allhallowtide season that was brought to the region by the Spanish; the Day of the Dead has become a way to remember those forebears of Mexican culture.

cultural_events.name: Guelaguetza
cultural_events.writeup: An indigenous cultural event in Oaxaca featuring traditional dances, music, and costumes.

wiki.extract: The Guelaguetza, also known as Los lunes del cerro, is an annual indigenous cultural event in Mexico that takes place in the city of Oaxaca, capital of the state of Oaxaca, and nearby villages. The celebration features traditional costumed dancing by gender-separated groups. It includes native food, and statewide artisanal crafts, such as pre-Hispanic style textiles. Each costume, or traje, and dance usually has a local indigenous historical and cultural meaning. While the celebration has attracted an increasing number of tourists, it is primarily one of deep cultural importance for the indigenous peoples of the state and is important for the survival of these cultures.

cultural_events.name: Cinco de Mayo
cultural_events.writeup: Commemorates the Mexican army's victory over French forces at the Battle of Puebla.

wiki.extract: Cinco de Mayo is an annual celebration held on May 5 to celebrate Mexico's victory over the Second French Empire at the Battle of Puebla in 1862, led by General Ignacio Zaragoza. Zaragoza died months after the battle from an illness, however, and a larger French force ultimately defeated the Mexican army at the Second Battle of Puebla and then occupied Mexico City. Following the end of the American Civil War in 1865, the United States began lending money and guns to the Mexican Liberals, pushing France and Mexican Conservatives to the edge of defeat. At the opening of the French chambers in January 1866, Napoleon III announced that he would withdraw French troops from Mexico. In reply to a French request for American neutrality, the American secretary of state William H. Seward replied that French withdrawal from Mexico should be unconditional.

cultural_events.name: Semana Santa
cultural_events.writeup: Holy Week celebrations with religious processions and ceremonies across the country.

wiki.extract: Semana Santa is the Spanish for Holy Week, the final week of Lent leading to Easter. In Spanish speaking cultures as well as the Philippines this becomes an annual tribute of the Passion of Jesus Christ celebrated by Catholic religious brotherhoods and confraternities that process on the streets of many Spanish speaking towns and cities during Holy Week. In some parts of Latin America it became part of the acculturation of pre conquest beliefs into Catholic culture.

cultural_events.name: Festival Internacional Cervantino
cultural_events.writeup: An annual arts festival in Guanajuato showcasing music, theater, and dance from around the world.

wiki.extract: The Festival Internacional Cervantino (FIC), popularly known as El Cervantino, is a festival which takes place each fall in the city of Guanajuato, located in central Mexico. The festival originates from the mid 20th century, when short plays by Miguel de Cervantes called entremeses were performed in the city's plazas.

food_writeup: Mexican cuisine is known for its bold flavors and diverse ingredients, including corn, beans, chili peppers, and avocados. Popular dishes include tacos, mole, tamales, and enchiladas, reflecting a blend of indigenous and Spanish influences.
brief_history: Mexico has a rich history dating back to advanced pre-Columbian civilizations like the Maya and Aztec. It was colonized by Spain in the 16th century and gained independence in 1821. The country has since undergone political and social transformations, becoming a federal republic with a diverse cultural heritage.

commentary.inflation_management: Banco de Mexico has run a 3% inflation target since 2001 and is one of the most credible emerging-market central banks. Inflation stayed in the 3.4-5.3% range through the 2010s, with its low point at 2.7% in 2015. The sharpest breach came in 2017, when inflation hit 6.0% after the peso's post-2016 US election depreciation and the fuel-price liberalization (gasolinazo); the bank hiked steadily and restored control. The global post-COVID shock pushed inflation to a period high of 7.9% in 2022, and the bank tightened aggressively again, bringing it down to 4.7% in 2024 and a projected 3.8% in 2025. The peso's floating regime absorbs external shocks, but pass-through from the exchange rate and US prices keeps the bank on constant guard.
commentary.debt_management: Mexico's debt story is one of slow but persistent ratcheting: gross debt rose from 35.8% of GDP in 2006 to a projected 61.8% in 2025, nearly doubling. The GFC hit Mexico harder than most peers (GDP fell from $1.16tn in 2008 to $943bn in 2009, amplified by peso depreciation), yet debt only ticked up to 41.7%; the bigger climb came in 2013-2016, when falling oil prices and Pemex's deteriorating finances pushed it from 40.8% to 55.0%. Mexico notably kept its COVID fiscal response small by emerging-market standards, so debt rose only to 58.5% in 2020, but the Lopez Obrador years then added fiscal pressure through energy subsidies and flagship projects, taking debt to its projected 61.8% high. With oil revenues weaker and rates high, the fiscal space built up over two decades has largely been spent.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis: Mexico suffered one of the sharpest GFC contractions in the region; GDP fell to $943bn in 2009.
Constitutional energy reform ended Pemex's 75-year upstream monopoly, opening oil, gas and power to private investment (constitutional amendment published December 2013).
The peso slid sharply after the 2016 US presidential election on NAFTA termination threats; inflation later spiked to 6.0% in 2017.
Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador won the presidency in July 2018 on an anti-neoliberal platform, taking office that December.
COVID-19: GDP fell to $1.12tn; Mexico's fiscal response was deliberately restrained, keeping debt to 58.5%.
USMCA entered force in July 2020; post-COVID inflation peaked at 7.9% in 2022 as Banxico hiked.
Claudia Sheinbaum elected president in June 2024; GDP reached a projected $1.83tn in 2025, with debt at its 61.8% high.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is nearshoring-driven investment growth, inflation converging to target, and debt stabilizing just above 60% of GDP, provided the Sheinbaum administration restores some fiscal discipline. The upside is real: USMCA access and supply-chain diversification make Mexico a natural winner from friend-shoring. The risks are US tariff escalation under the Trump administration, Pemex's massive liabilities and declining output, and security costs. Mexico's institutional strength (independent Banxico) is a backstop, but fiscal reform is the missing piece.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
